The figure uses the existing state variable from the
[COAT data portal](https://data.coat.no/state-variable/c101_annual_mean_air_temperature_weather_stations_v1).

The figure is interactive. You can:

- Hover over points to inspect values.
- Zoom and pan.
- Hide or show regions using the legend.
- Reset the view using the plot controls.

## Source and attribution

This document is based on the existing plotting script:

```text
state_variable_figure_v85_dwarf_shrub_abundance.Rmd
```
by Hanna Bohner.

The original script was adapted to:

- Use Quarto and HTML output.
- Create an interactive Plotly figure.
- Use the existing state variable from the COAT data portal.
- Avoid saving figures to Box.
- Avoid installing packages while rendering.
- Avoid uploading or modifying data on the COAT data portal.
- Produce an output suitable for later publication through GitHub Pages.

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

required_packages <- c(
  "ckanr",
  "dplyr",
  "plotly"
)

missing_packages <- required_packages[
  !vapply(
    required_packages,
    requireNamespace,
    quietly = TRUE,
    FUN.VALUE = logical(1)
  )
]

if (length(missing_packages) > 0L) {
  stop(
    "The following R packages are missing: ",
    paste(missing_packages, collapse = ", "),
    ". Install them once before rendering this document."
  )
}

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(ckanr)
  library(dplyr)
  library(plotly)
})

source(
  "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/COATnor/data_management_scripts/master/download_data_from_coat_data_portal.R"
)

if (!nzchar(Sys.getenv("api_COAT"))) {
  stop(
    "The environment variable 'api_COAT' is not available. ",
    "Add it to your local .Renviron file before rendering."
  )
}

ckanr::ckanr_setup(
  url = "https://data.coat.no",
  key = Sys.getenv("api_COAT")
)
```

```{r}
#| label: download-data
#| include: false

# the splitting into historical and individual is an adaptation to the file structure for climate state variables

years_historical <- 1830:2025
#years_individual <- 2026:2028 # example for the years to come, when files containing data from only one year are added

filename_historical <- paste0("C101_annual_mean_air_temperature_weather_stations_",
                              min(years_historical), "_", max(years_historical), ".txt")
#filenames_individual <- paste0("C101_annual_mean_air_temperature_weather_stations_", years_individual, ".txt") #for the years to come

filenames <- filename_historical
#filenames <- c(filename_historical, filenames_individual) #for the years to come


dat_list <- download_coat_data(
  name = "c101_annual_mean_air_temperature_weather_stations_v1",
  filenames = filenames,
  store = "session"
)

if (length(dat_list) == 0L) {
  stop("No data were downloaded.")
}

dat <- dplyr::bind_rows(dat_list)

if (nrow(dat) == 0L) {
  stop("The downloaded data contain no rows.")
}
```


```{r}

#| label: prepare-data
#| include: false

# Extract all years from filenames
years_in_filenames <- stringr::str_extract_all(
  filenames,
  "\\d{4}"
) |>
  unlist() |>
  as.numeric()

first_year <- min(years_in_filenames, na.rm = TRUE)
last_year  <- max(years_in_filenames, na.rm = TRUE)


region_codes <- c(
  "svalbard",
  "troms",
  "varanger"
)

region_labels <- c(
  svalbard = "Svalbard",
  troms = "Troms",
  varanger = "Varanger"
)

region_colours <- c(
  "Svalbard" = "#468f9b",
  "Troms" = "#df8600",
  "Varanger" = "#925A00"
)

# Calculate annual regional mean and 95% confidence intervals
dat_plot <- dat |>
  dplyr::filter(
    sn_region %in% region_codes
  ) |>
  dplyr::group_by(
    sn_region,
    t_year
  ) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    n = sum(!is.na(v_temperature_year)),

    temperature_mean = if (n > 0) {
      mean(v_temperature_year, na.rm = TRUE)
    } else {
      NA_real_
    },

    standard_deviation = if (n > 1) {
      sd(v_temperature_year, na.rm = TRUE)
    } else {
      NA_real_
    },

    standard_error = standard_deviation / sqrt(n),

    t_critical = if (n > 1) {
      stats::qt(0.975, df = n - 1)
    } else {
      NA_real_
    },

    lower_ci = temperature_mean -
      t_critical * standard_error,

    upper_ci = temperature_mean +
      t_critical * standard_error,

    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    full_region = unname(region_labels[sn_region]),

    colour = unname(region_colours[full_region]),

    hover_text = paste0(
      "<br>Region: ", full_region,
      "<br>Year: ", t_year,
      "<br>Mean temperature: ",
      round(temperature_mean, 2), " ??C",
      "<br>Upper 95% CI: ",
      round(upper_ci, 2), " ??C",
      "<br>Lower 95% CI: ",
      round(lower_ci, 2), " ??C",
      "<br>Number of stations: ", n
    )
  )

```



```{r}

#| label: interactive-figure
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6


# Set y-axis limits based on the confidence intervals
y_min <- min(dat_plot$lower_ci, na.rm = TRUE)
y_max <- max(dat_plot$upper_ci, na.rm = TRUE)

# Fallback if confidence intervals are unavailable
if (!is.finite(y_min)) {
  y_min <- min(dat_plot$temperature_mean, na.rm = TRUE)
}

if (!is.finite(y_max)) {
  y_max <- max(dat_plot$temperature_mean, na.rm = TRUE)
}

# Add 10% padding to the y-axis
y_range <- y_max - y_min

if (!is.finite(y_range) || y_range == 0) {
  y_range <- 1
}

y_axis_min <- y_min - y_range * 0.05
y_axis_max <- y_max + y_range * 0.05


######################################################


# Sort data by region and year
dat_plot <- dat_plot |>
  dplyr::arrange(full_region, t_year)

region_present <- unique(dat_plot$full_region)

p <- plotly::plot_ly()

# First: draw confidence interval polygons
for (region_name in region_present) {

  region_data <- dat_plot |>
    dplyr::filter(
      full_region == region_name,
      !is.na(lower_ci),
      !is.na(upper_ci),
      is.finite(lower_ci),
      is.finite(upper_ci)
    ) |>
    dplyr::arrange(t_year)

  region_colour <- unique(region_data$colour)

  if (nrow(region_data) > 1) {

    # Construct a closed polygon:
    # lower CI forward, upper CI backwards
    polygon_x <- c(
      region_data$t_year,
      rev(region_data$t_year)
    )

    polygon_y <- c(
      region_data$lower_ci,
      rev(region_data$upper_ci)
    )

    p <- p |>
      plotly::add_trace(
        x = polygon_x,
        y = polygon_y,
        type = "scatter",
        mode = "lines",
        fill = "toself",
        fillcolor = grDevices::adjustcolor(
          region_colour,
          alpha.f = 0.15
        ),
        line = list(
          color = "rgba(0,0,0,0)",
          width = 0
        ),
        name = paste0(region_name, " 95% CI"),
        legendgroup = region_name,
        hoverinfo = "skip",
        showlegend = FALSE,
        inherit = FALSE
      )
  }
}

# Second: draw annual mean temperature lines
for (region_name in region_present) {

  region_data <- dat_plot |>
    dplyr::filter(full_region == region_name) |>
    dplyr::arrange(t_year)

  region_colour <- unique(region_data$colour)

  p <- p |>
    plotly::add_trace(
      data = region_data,
      x = ~t_year,
      y = ~temperature_mean,
      type = "scatter",
      mode = "lines+markers",
      name = region_name,
      legendgroup = region_name,
      line = list(
        color = region_colour,
        width = 3
      ),
      marker = list(
        color = region_colour,
        size = 5
      ),
      text = ~hover_text,
      hoverinfo = "text",
      inherit = FALSE
    )
}



######################################################


# Create decade labels for the initial x-axis view
decade_ticks <- seq(first_year, last_year, by = 10)

p |>
  plotly::layout(
    title = list(
      text = "Annual mean air temperature by region"
    ),

    xaxis = list(
      title = "Year",
      range = c(first_year, last_year),
      dtick = 10
    ),

    yaxis = list(
      title = "Temperature (??C)",
      range = c(y_axis_min, y_axis_max),
      tickformat = ".1f",
      zeroline = TRUE
    ),

    hovermode = "x unified",

    legend = list(
      title = list(text = "Region")
    )
  ) |>
  plotly::config(
    displaylogo = FALSE,
    responsive = TRUE,
    modeBarButtonsToRemove = c(
      "lasso2d",
      "select2d"
    )
  )

```



::: {.figure-caption}

**Annual mean air temperature for Svalbard, Troms and Varanger.** Calculations are based on historical weather station data from [Frost](https://frost.met.no/index.html) by MET Norway. Visit the [COAT data portal](https://data.coat.no/state-variable/c101_annual_mean_air_temperature_weather_stations_v1) for more information about the dataset.

:::
## Data and provenance

The data were downloaded from the COAT data portal using the existing state
variable:

```text
c101_annual_mean_air_temperature_weather_stations_v1
```

The following filters were applied:

- Years included: `1830` to `2025`

The figure is generated from an existing unpublished state variable on the COAT Data Portal. This
document does not calculate a new state-variable version, upload files, or
modify metadata on the COAT data portal.
